title: Google Will Switch AI Off by Default for K-12 Student Accounts
summary: Google says Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Google Search will be off for K-12 student accounts until a school administrator turns them on, with details to come before the change rolls out. At the same time, Guided Learning, Gemini's step-by-step study mode, is now available in Google Classroom worldwide.
body:
On November 3 Google announced a change to how schools get its AI. For K-12 student accounts, access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Google Search will be turned off by default and will stay off until the school's administrator explicitly enables it. Google says it will share more details with schools in the coming months, before the change takes effect; it has not given a date.

Guided Learning comes to Classroom

The same post moves Guided Learning, Gemini's study mode, into Google Classroom. Instead of handing over an answer, it coaches a student through a problem with open questions and step-by-step explanations. Teachers assign it as an activity tied to their class material and see in real time where the class is struggling. It is available globally from the day of the announcement.

And into Search, as a pilot

Google is also building Guided Learning into Search for student accounts. When Search recognizes certain homework questions, it will walk the student through the topic rather than giving the answer outright. A pilot starts later in November in selected US schools, with other districts to follow in the coming months.

Who it matters to

School IT administrators are the ones who will decide what students can use, so the default matters most to them. For parents and teachers it means that a school account may no longer come with AI switched on.

What this means if you choose AI for studying

If you are a teacher in a school on Google Workspace, talk to your administrator now: once the new default applies, Gemini tools for students will only work if the school turns them on.

If you want a tutor that explains rather than answers, Guided Learning joins tools built around the same idea, such as Khanmigo. For studying from your own notes, see NotebookLM, and for the full list, our AI tools for learning.
